SMTO-EXE-0060 — The computer didn't bring that window to the front

GUID: a8052da8-2d10-5f70-bb12-5dfb05b822fb
Slug: desktop-focus-denied
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: desktop

What happened

  • SMTO asked the Gateway computer to switch to a window, but the computer refused or the window didn't end up in front. The window may still have changed partly, for example by being restored.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the Gateway computer, click the window you want so it comes to the front. Operating systems often let only a person, not a background program, switch the active window.
  2. Make sure the computer is unlocked and no dialog box is covering the window. A lock screen or pop-up can keep another window from coming to the front.
  3. Ask SMTO which window is active now (for example "which window is in front?") before continuing. This confirms the right window is in front before any step that depends on it.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the window you wanted as the active window.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer. Don't keep asking SMTO to switch windows over and over; check which window is in front first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Foreground activation was refused by the native API, or post-action observation did not confirm the requested window gained focus; the check does not establish the OS's exact reason, and the effect may be partial.

What this means

  • Native activation was refused or post-action window observation did not confirm that the requested window became focused. The check does not establish the OS's exact reason. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • Native activation was refused or post-action window observation did not confirm that the requested window became focused. The check does not establish the OS's exact reason.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the intended window's current focus and session state; distinguish refusal from a vanished or unobservable target.

How to fix it

  • Activate the target through normal OS interaction (Windows foreground-lock rules, macOS activation policy, or the X11 window manager may refuse programmatic focus), then confirm with desktop.active_window that the exact window_id is focused before sending focus-dependent input. Receipts may carry effect_unknown=true.
  • Activate the intended application through normal OS interaction, then verify which window has focus.

Retry and execution caution

  • Activate the application manually or allow foreground activation through normal OS interaction, then inspect the active window.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact intended window is observed as focused before sending focus-dependent input.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass identity protection or automatically replay an uncertain mutation.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
